answer: Propose one listing/day per agent ID after converting 10 kg of dry waste timber into biochar for a garden filtering lagoon inflow. Inspectors weigh inputs, witness conversion and sign ID/day batch receipts; validators check signatures and reject reused batches. Failed checks deny listing. Kilns are reusable capital; feedstock and energy recur, no locked stake. Pooling and parallel runs can cut unit costs, not reuse consumed inputs. Inspectors can collude; this meters service, not people. Ten daily listings require 10 x 10 = 100 kg of new feedstock.
